nodes.name: Kessler Reservoir pipeline
nodes.summary:
The Harbor Vale Water Authority (HVWA) is responsible for the Kessler Reservoir pipeline, which was built in 1961.
Harbor Vale Water Authority owns Kessler Reservoir pipeline The Kessler Reservoir pipeline was built in 1961. It is the subject of a modernization plan involving a 9 percent tariff increase, a 60 million dollar loan from the Coastal Infrastructure Bank, and a revised proposal by Nadia Okafor that includes discounts for low-income households. The pipeline study for the replacement project cost 4.2 million dollars and was conducted by Brightline Consulting, a firm owned by Marco Reyes, the brother of former HVWA chief executive Tomas Reyes. Grace Lindqvist's audit in June found that the Brightline contract broke procurement rules, though no evidence suggested Tomas Reyes personally profited. The Harbor Vale Water Authority, led by acting chief executive Nadia Okafor, committed to publishing every pipeline contract to restore public trust ahead of the city council vote on 15 July.

nodes.name: Nadia Okafor
nodes.summary: Nadia Okafor was appointed as acting chief executive of the Authority. Chief engineer Nadia Okafor was appointed acting chief executive of the Harbor Vale Water Authority on 28 March following the resignation of Tomas Reyes. She stated she would publish every pipeline contract.

nodes.name: Harbor Vale
nodes.summary:
Harbor Vale is a city facing a water tariff controversy involving the Harbor Vale Water Authority (HVWA). The city's largest newspaper, the Harbor Vale Courier, published an investigation revealing HVWA paid $4.2 million to Brightline Consulting for a pipeline study. State auditor Grace Lindqvist opened a formal audit of HVWA in March, finding the Brightline contract broke procurement rules, though no evidence showed HVWA chief executive Tomas Reyes personally profited. HVWA resigned Reyes as chief executive on 28 March and appointed chief engineer Nadia Okafor as acting chief executive. Mayor Ilse Varga withdrew support for an 18 percent tariff increase on 2 April, calling for a pause to rebuild public trust. In May, Okafor presented a revised plan cutting the tariff rise to 9 percent with a discount for income-support households, funded by a $60 million loan from the Coastal Infrastructure Bank.

nodes.name: Harbor Vale Water Authority
nodes.summary:
The Harbor Vale Water Authority (HVWA) supplies drinking water to Harbor Vale, a coastal city of 240,000 people. HVWA manages the Kessler Reservoir pipeline, built in 1961. Tomas Reyes served as chief executive until resigning on 28 March 2026 following an audit that found HVWA paid $4.2 million to Brightline Consulting for a pipeline study, a contract that broke procurement rules. Nadia Okafor, chief engineer, became acting chief executive and committed to publishing every pipeline contract. HVWA faces a city council vote on 15 July 2026 regarding a revised tariff plan that reduces the proposed 18 percent increase to 9 percent, includes a discount for low-income households, and requires a $60 million loan from the Coastal Infrastructure Bank. The Water Workers Union, led by Samuel Adeyemi, threatens a strike if the plan passes without a guarantee for 200 maintenance positions. The Tenants Alliance, led by Priya Raman, campaigns against shared meters in the Eastside district.
The Coastal Infrastructure Bank has provided $60 million for the Kessler Reservoir replacement.
